card.name: Breton dance
card.era: Traditional (some forms medieval); revived from the late 1950s
card.tagline: Umbrella of traditional Breton folk dances of the fest-noz.
card.profile: Breton dance is the umbrella of traditional dance forms from Brittany, the Celtic region of France, mostly social group dances in chains and circles (Wikipedia). Jean-Michel Guilcher identified five 'mother-forms' of Lower Brittany - the gavotte (dans tro), the en dro/an dro, the dans Treger, the dans Leon and the dans plinn - from which hundreds of terroir variants developed. Dances are performed at fest-noz (night festival) and fest-deiz (day festival), accompanied by kan-ha-diskan call-and-response singing or by sonneur duos and instruments such as the biniou (bagpipe), bombarde, accordion, clarinet (treujenn-gaol) and, via bagadou, the Scottish bagpipe. Revival came with the Celtic Circles and the modern fest-noz, credited especially to Loeiz Ropars from the 1950s.
card.insight: The fest-noz - 'festive gathering based on the collective practice of traditional dances of Brittany' - was inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List in 2012 (decision 7.COM 11.13; file 00707). UNESCO notes about a thousand fest-noz take place every year (UNESCO).
